A shameful experience. After being a regular customer, I will never set foot there again.
I have been a regular customer of this business, and for this very reason, what happened left me particularly disappointed.
During a grooming appointment for my dog, I arrived late and was informed that, for this reason, the service would not be performed. I understand the organizational problems caused by the delay, but what I cannot accept and consider totally unfair is that I was asked and charged the full amount for the service, even though the service was never performed.
Despite this, I personally tried to find a reasonable solution: I offered to pay the full amount anyway and to perform the grooming in September, upon my return from vacation.
So I was willing to pay for a service that I had not received at the time, and at the same time, I tried to accommodate the needs of the business.
The solution was not accepted: the money was collected, and the service was not performed.
I find this behavior unacceptable, unfair, and completely disrespectful toward a regular customer. A business may certainly have rules about appointments and lateness, but common sense and respect for the customer also matter.
What happened made me realize that, evidently, the relationship with the customer is less important than the revenue from the service.
After this experience, I will never return to this store and I absolutely cannot recommend it.
Losing a regular customer over a situation that could have been resolved simply with a little willingness and common sense is, in my opinion, an incomprehensible business decision.
For my part, the relationship is definitely over.

Reference to Mrs. Fioravanti's poodle review:
I'm replying from another account, unable to respond to Piccionetti's reply: 1) My dog ​​wasn't in terrible condition at all, not only because I brush him constantly, but above all because I've been bringing him to her every 20 days since September! And she herself opted for washing and grooming twice, advising me to get a haircut on the date I came, and she refused! 2) To prove her false reasons, she used a comb to pull out a knot in my poodle, making her cry and causing a hole in her hair, which I later checked at home and at another groomer I went to. And this is torture!!!! 3) She should know that despite the attention given to poodles, the situation can get worse in an instant, which is why we go to groomers! 4) In another center, the knots were untangled without damage in 2 and a half hours and without torture because I was present and the hair was cut short as I had asked her and not completely clipped!
The truth is that she didn't want to waste time because she has one mission! Profit! Sometimes even easy since she still demanded 55 euros, without doing absolutely anything and holding my dog ​​between Her arms until I took out my wallet!!! I'm the one who suffered damage with an outlay not due to her and another that I had to incur to pay another excellent groomer, plus the time wasted going there uselessly! After all, what can you expect from a center whose POS is almost always out of order and where you have to ask for the receipt on the way out that is absentmindedly forgotten??? Ms. Piccionetti, have the decency to remain silent and not provoke me needlessly, because I... prefer to forget you... and you should hope so too, I assure you!!!

A terrible experience. Forced to pay for a grooming service that wasn't provided because of the presence of knots (a completely normal thing for a poodle), the owner wanted to completely shave the dog, which I refused and wanted to leave. When she illegitimately asked me to pay 55 euros anyway, I then asked her to just wash it, or wash it and de-knot it, services that are still required for this breed of dog. The owner refused because de-knotting was considered animal torture (!! Removing all the hair, right?!!!!) and washing without de-knotting couldn't be done anyway! Responses that made no sense because these are services I've always used at any grooming shop. Why was I forced to pay? : Piccionetti had my dog ​​in her arms who was crying (she who talks about animal torture!!!!) and when I started to dispute the undue profit she was demanding, she backed away into the area where I was not allowed to enter... she only gave the dog back when I took out my wallet! Clearly, I wasn't in a position to descend to her level, nor, unfortunately, did I have time to request and wait for external intervention (Financial Police, Municipal Police) to explain to the owner the financial abuse she was committing, and has committed. She could have washed the dog for the same price as the haircut, since I was the one who suggested it, and I was always the one who accepted it being returned with the knots she alleged. Moreover, I had been to her 20 days earlier for a wash and grooming; such a tragic situation after such a short time is impossible, unless the work had already been done poorly 20 days earlier. I should add that we're talking about a very small toy poodle, which I brush
regularly. You want an easy win, Mrs. Piccionetti, only poodles without knots or shorn like sheep!
